title: Solids, Liquids, and Change
objectives: I can tell a solid from a liquid.
I can tell what happens when something melts, freezes, or boils.
I can say if something floats, sinks, or dissolves in water.
I can predict and notice a change, then tell what I saw.
rationale: Second graders watch these changes in class: ice melting, water freezing, sugar disappearing into tea, and objects floating or sinking in a tub. The eight words name the two kinds of matter children compare (solid, liquid), the changes heat and cold cause (melt, freeze, boil), and what happens to things placed in water (float, sink, dissolve). Each word can be shown with a real object, so children test, notice, and say what happened. The unit revisits predict, notice, fact, and label because every investigation starts with a prediction and ends with labeled observations.

passage.title: Matter and Change
paras: Ice is a solid, but when the sun warms it, it will melt into a liquid. In a cold freezer, the water will freeze again. A grown-up can boil water until it bubbles.
A toy boat will float on the water, but a stone will sink. Sugar will dissolve when you stir it into warm tea.

choices: change from a solid to a liquid
qs.why: Ice is a solid, and the sun warms it into a liquid, so it melts.

qs.q: What happens to a stone in water?
qs.why: The text says a stone will sink.

qs.q: What can a grown-up do to water until it bubbles?
qs.why: The text says a grown-up can boil water until it bubbles.

teacher.overview: Children learn eight science words for matter and change and use them in simple tests with real objects. Always use the pattern predict, test, notice, and say what happened. Revisit predict, notice, fact, and label with each test. A grown-up must do all heating, and no child heats anything.

notes.va.solid.n: A solid keeps its shape. Use blocks, ice, and spoons. Children may think powders like sugar are not solids; each grain is solid. Cognate sólido.
notes.va.liquid.n: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container. Use a cup and a bowl. Children may think thick liquids like honey are solids; show that honey flows.
notes.va.melt.v: Melt needs heat and goes from solid to liquid. Use ice in a warm place and in a cold place. Link the melting of ice to the idea of a prediction.
notes.va.freeze.v: Freeze needs cold and goes from liquid to solid. Use ice cube trays in a freezer if available. Freeze is also a movement word; teach the science sense.
notes.va.boil.v: Boil is a grown-up demonstration only; show with a picture or a video, not children near hot water. Contrast with melt and freeze.
notes.va.float.v: Float means to stay on top. Children often think big things always sink; test a big light object and a small heavy one. Remember that float can be in air for balloons.
notes.va.sink.v: Sink means to go down in water. The noun sink in a kitchen is a different word; teach only the verb. Past forms sank and sunk are irregular; model them in speech.
notes.va.dissolve.v: Dissolve means a solid mixes into a liquid and seems to disappear. Use sugar and salt in warm water, stirred by an adult or child with supervision. Sand does not dissolve. Cognate disolver.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I predict the wooden block will float because it is light. I drop it in the water and notice that it stays on top. My prediction was right. Wood floats and a stone sinks, so I can label them in a chart.'
discuss: What did you predict and what did you notice?
Which of these changes can be undone, and which cannot?
misconceptions: Children may think dissolve means melt. Melt is a solid changing with heat; dissolve is a solid mixing into a liquid.
Some children think all big things sink and all small things float. Test and compare.
Children may say the ice disappeared when it melted. It turned into water.
extend: Run a float or sink test with ten classroom objects and record the results in a chart.
Draw before and after pictures of ice melting.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit predict, notice, fact, and label in every test: predict first, notice what happens, record a fact, and label the chart.

wida.oral: Hold up an object. Tell your partner if it is a solid or a liquid and predict if it will float or sink.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (sólido, líquido, derretir, congelar, hervir, flotar, hundirse, disolver) not reviewed by a native speaker.
Science facts to check: ice melts with heat; water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius; sugar and salt dissolve in water and sand does not; the boil activity is teacher-led only.
